cards.gokturk-devleti-552.title: The Göktürk state declared its independence in 552
cards.gokturk-devleti-552.body: Bumin destroyed the Juan-Juan (Rouran) state, and the independent Göktürk state was founded in 552. Bumin, who took the title Il Khagan, died in the first year after its founding. The state's name was actually Türk, not Kök-Türk; in the inscriptions it was sometimes written as Türük.
cards.orhon-yazitlari.title: Orkhon Inscriptions: Kül Tigin and Bilge Khagan
cards.orhon-yazitlari.body: Among the inscriptions near the Orkhon River in central Mongolia, the Kül Tigin inscription is thought to have been erected in 732 and the Bilge Khagan inscription in 735. The person who carved these two inscriptions into stone was their nephew, Yollug Tigin. The two great inscriptions use 38 letters.
cards.uygur-kaganligi.title: The Uyghur Khaganate: from Manichaeism to Turfan
cards.uygur-kaganligi.body: The Uyghur Khaganate, which flourished under Bögü Khagan, who officially adopted Manichaeism, came to an end with the Kyrgyz attack of 840. The most brilliant period of Uyghur literature began after this date, when the Uyghurs settled in Turfan and Gansu.
cards.satuk-bugra-han-karahanlilar.title: Satuq Bughra Khan and the Karakhanids
cards.satuk-bugra-han-karahanlilar.body: Satuq, of the Karakhanid dynasty, became a Muslim in 920 or 945 and took the name Abdulkarim. Satuq Bughra Khan worked to spread Islam in the western lands of the Karakhanids. He died in 955 and was buried in Artush, near Kashgar.
cards.dandanakan-savasi-1040.title: The Battle of Dandanaqan and the Great Seljuk Empire
cards.dandanakan-savasi-1040.body: In the Battle of Dandanaqan, which ended on May 23, 1040, the Seljuks dealt the Ghaznavid army a decisive defeat. On the last day of the battle, the Seljuk beys proclaimed Tughril Bey the first sultan of the new state. This marked the founding of the Great Seljuk Empire.
cards.malazgirt-muharebesi-1071.title: The Battle of Manzikert: August 26, 1071
cards.malazgirt-muharebesi-1071.body: On August 26, 1071, the Seljuk army under the command of Alp Arslan inflicted a heavy defeat on the Byzantine army at Manzikert (Malazgirt); Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes was taken prisoner. After this victory, the Turks advanced into the interior of Anatolia without meeting significant resistance.
cards.istanbul-kusatmasi-1453.title: The conquest of Istanbul: a 54-day siege
cards.istanbul-kusatmasi-1453.body: Mehmed II's siege of Istanbul (Constantinople) lasted 54 days, from April 6 to May 29, 1453. The Boğazkesen fortress (Rumelihisarı), completed before the siege, was meant to cut the city off from its supply centers on the Black Sea and to secure the passage of fleets between Anatolia and Rumelia.
cards.kanuni-sultan-suleyman.title: The longest-reigning sultan: Suleiman the Lawgiver
cards.kanuni-sultan-suleyman.body: Suleiman the Lawgiver (Kanuni Sultan Suleiman, 1520–1566), whose reign lasted 46 years by the Gregorian calendar, is the sultan who stayed on the throne the longest in Ottoman history. Western writers of his time referred to him by the epithet “the Magnificent.”
cards.piri-reis-dunya-haritasi-1513.body: The surviving fragment of the 1513 world map that Piri Reis drew in Gallipoli shows the coasts of Spain, Portugal, and West Africa, along with the eastern coasts of the Americas. The map's sources include a map by Christopher Columbus.
cards.ilk-turk-matbaasi.title: The first Turkish printing press and the Vankulu Dictionary
cards.ilk-turk-matbaasi.body: In 1727, a decree issued by Ahmed III gave Ibrahim Müteferrika and Mehmed Said Efendi permission to set up the first Turkish printing press. The press's first book was the Vankulu Dictionary, whose printing was completed in 1729. By the time of Müteferrika's death, 17 books (23 volumes) had been printed.
cards.tanzimat-fermani-1839.title: The Tanzimat Edict: November 3, 1839
cards.tanzimat-fermani-1839.body: On November 3, 1839, Foreign Minister Mustafa Reshid Pasha read out the Tanzimat Edict at Gülhane Square. According to the edict, new laws would be based on the security of life, the protection of property, honor, and dignity, the regulation of taxes, and the reform of military conscription.
cards.kanun-i-esasi-1876.title: The first Ottoman constitution: the Kanun-i Esasi
cards.kanun-i-esasi-1876.body: On December 23, 1876, the Kanun-i Esasi was proclaimed, the first constitution in Ottoman history. Under the constitution, the General Assembly (Meclis-i Umumi) consisted of two chambers: the Chamber of Deputies (Heyet-i Mebusan) and the Senate (Heyet-i Ayan). After working for two terms, the assembly was suspended in 1878 until the Second Constitutional Era.
cards.tbmm-acilisi-1920.title: The Grand National Assembly of Türkiye opened on April 23, 1920
cards.tbmm-acilisi-1920.body: The Grand National Assembly of Türkiye opened on April 23, 1920. Three days later, on April 26, 1920, the Assembly set up its own administrative structure by adopting the 1916 rules of procedure of the Ottoman Chamber of Deputies (Meclis-i Mebusan) with some amendments.
cards.cumhuriyetin-ilani-1923.title: October 29, 1923: The form of government is a republic
cards.cumhuriyetin-ilani-1923.body: With an amendment adopted by the Grand National Assembly on October 29, 1923, the statement “The form of government of the State of Türkiye is a republic.” was added to the first article of the 1921 Constitution. In the election held afterward, Mustafa Kemal Pasha was elected the first president of the Republic of Türkiye.
cards.lozan-antlasmasi-1923.title: The Treaty of Lausanne: July 24, 1923
cards.lozan-antlasmasi-1923.body: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed on July 24, 1923, at a ceremony held in the hall of the University of Lausanne. The treaty is not a single text; it consists of the main peace treaty of 143 articles and 17 separate protocols or conventions attached to it.
cards.uc-mart-1924-kanunlari.title: March 3, 1924: The caliphate and unified education
cards.uc-mart-1924-kanunlari.body: In its session of March 3, 1924, the Grand National Assembly adopted the Law on the Unification of Education (Tevhid-i Tedrisat) and Law No. 431, which abolished the caliphate. The Law on the Unification of Education brought all instruction together to create a single education system in place of the dual one.
cards.kadinlarin-secme-secilme-hakki.tit: Women's right to vote and stand for election
cards.kadinlarin-secme-secilme-hakki.bod: Turkish women were granted the right to vote and stand for election in municipal elections on April 3, 1930, and in elections for village headmen and councils of elders on October 26, 1933. On December 5, 1934, they gained the right to vote and stand for election to parliament.
cards.soyadi-kanunu-1934.title: The Surname Law and the surname Atatürk
cards.soyadi-kanunu-1934.body: The Surname Law, enacted on June 21, 1934, required every citizen to bear a family surname in addition to their given name. Mustafa Kemal was given the surname “Atatürk” by a law passed by the Grand National Assembly on November 24, 1934.
cards.agri-dagi.title: Mount Ararat: Türkiye's highest volcanic mountain
cards.agri-dagi.body: Mount Ararat (Ağrı Dağı) is a volcanic massif made up of two cones, Greater Ararat and Lesser Ararat. Greater Ararat is 5137 m high, and Lesser Ararat is 3896 m. The part of the mountain above 4000 meters is permanently covered with snow, and there is a glacier at its summit.
cards.turkiyenin-en-buyuk-golleri.title: Türkiye's largest lakes
cards.turkiyenin-en-buyuk-golleri.body: According to data from the State Hydraulic Works (DSİ), Türkiye's largest lakes are Lake Van (3,713 km²), Lake Tuz (1,300 km²), Lake Beyşehir (656 km²), and Lake Eğirdir (482 km²). The number of natural lakes identified in the country is 320.
cards.turkiyenin-komsulari.title: Türkiye's neighbors
cards.turkiyenin-komsulari.body: Türkiye shares borders with Greece and Bulgaria to the west; Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan (Nakhchivan), and Iran to the east; and Syria and Iraq to the south. According to the State Hydraulic Works (DSİ), the country is made up of 25 river basins.
cards.yedi-cografi-bolge-1941.title: The seven geographical regions were defined in 1941
cards.yedi-cografi-bolge-1941.body: At the First Geography Congress, held in Ankara on June 6–21, 1941, the 19-member Geography of Türkiye Commission divided Türkiye into 7 major geographical regions based on natural and human criteria. Along with scientists, the commission included a representative of the General Directorate of Mapping.
cards.il-yuzolcumleri-konya-yalova.title: Of the 81 provinces, Konya is the largest and Yalova the smallest
cards.il-yuzolcumleri-konya-yalova.body: According to the 2026 calculation by the General Directorate of Mapping (HGM), the largest of the 81 provinces by area is Konya (40,824 km²) and the smallest is Yalova (799 km²). These figures are nominal and are updated by the HGM every year.
cards.kapadokya-peribacalari.title: The fairy chimneys of Cappadocia
cards.kapadokya-peribacalari.body: Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia lie in a volcanic landscape shaped by erosion on the Central Anatolian plateau. The landscape features ridges, valleys, and rock pillars known as “fairy chimneys.” The site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1985.
cards.tdk-kurulusu-1932.title: The Turkish Language Association was founded on July 12, 1932
cards.tdk-kurulusu-1932.body: The Turkish Language Association was founded on July 12, 1932, on Atatürk's instructions, under the name Society for the Study of the Turkish Language (Türk Dili Tetkik Cemiyeti). The society was renamed the Turkish Language Research Association at its 1934 congress and the Turkish Language Association at its 1936 congress.
cards.dil-bayrami-26-eylul.title: Why is September 26 Language Day?
cards.dil-bayrami-26-eylul.body: The First Turkish Language Congress convened on September 26, 1932, at Dolmabahçe Palace with Atatürk in attendance. It was proposed that September 26, the first day of the congress, be celebrated every year as “Language Day,” and the proposal was accepted unanimously.
cards.divanu-lugatit-turk.title: Mahmud al-Kashgari's Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk
cards.divanu-lugatit-turk.body: Mahmud al-Kashgari wrote the Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk in 1072–1074 to teach Turkish to Arabs. In the work, the headwords are in Turkish and the explanations are in Arabic. The only known manuscript copy is kept in the Millet Library in Fatih, Istanbul.
cards.kutadgu-bilig.title: Kutadgu Bilig: “The knowledge of attaining happiness”
cards.kutadgu-bilig.body: Yusuf Khass Hajib wrote the Kutadgu Bilig in Balasagun, completed it in Kashgar, and presented it in 1069–70 to the Karakhanid ruler Tabghach Ulugh Bughra Khan. The title of the work means “the knowledge of attaining happiness.”
cards.harf-inkilabi-1928.title: The new Turkish letters: Law No. 1353
cards.harf-inkilabi-1928.body: The Law on the Adoption and Implementation of the New Turkish Letters was passed unanimously on November 1, 1928, and took effect when it was published in the Official Gazette on November 3. From January 1, 1929, government offices were required to use the Turkish letters.
cards.thomsen-orhon-yazitlari.title: The linguist who deciphered the Orkhon inscriptions: Thomsen
cards.thomsen-orhon-yazitlari.body: Danish linguist Vilhelm Thomsen deciphered the language of the inscribed stones along the Orkhon and Yenisei rivers and proved that they had been left by the Turks. Thomsen announced his discovery in a paper on December 15, 1893.
cards.turk-kahvesi-kulturu.title: Turkish coffee culture on the UNESCO list
cards.turk-kahvesi-kulturu.body: Freshly roasted beans are ground into a fine powder; the coffee, cold water, and sugar are put into a cezve (coffee pot) and brewed slowly on the stove. It is served in small cups with a glass of water. Turkish coffee culture and tradition were added to the UNESCO Representative List in 2013.
cards.karagoz-golge-oyunu.title: Karagöz shadow play
cards.karagoz-golge-oyunu.body: Karagöz is a shadow play in which figures made of camel or ox hide are held on rods in front of a light source so that their shadows fall on a cotton screen. Its main characters are Karagöz and Hacivat. It was added to the UNESCO Representative List in 2009.
cards.islik-dili-kusdili.title: Bird language: Giresun's whistled language
cards.islik-dili-kusdili.body: The whistled language is widely used in the districts of Giresun, above all Çanakçı, as well as Görele, Eynesil, and Tirebolu. It is estimated that nearly 10,000 people in the eastern Black Sea region can speak or understand it. In 2017, it was inscribed on UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding.
cards.ebru-sanati.title: Ebru: the art of patterns on water
cards.ebru-sanati.body: Ebru is a traditional Turkish art in which paints are sprinkled onto the surface of a trough of thickened water and spread with a brush, and the resulting patterns are transferred onto paper. A few drops of ox gall are added to the natural pigments. It was added to the UNESCO Representative List in 2014.
cards.gobekli-tepe.title: Göbekli Tepe: 9600–8200 BCE
cards.gobekli-tepe.body: At Göbekli Tepe, in the Germuş Mountains of southeastern Anatolia, stand monumental megalithic structures erected by hunter-gatherers between 9600 and 8200 BCE. The T-shaped pillars bear depictions of wild animals. The site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018.
cards.selimiye-camii-kulliyesi.title: Selimiye: the complex Sinan considered his finest work
cards.selimiye-camii-kulliyesi.body: The Selimiye Mosque and its Social Complex in Edirne were commissioned by Selim II. Sinan, the most famous Ottoman architect of the 16th century, regarded this complex, with its madrasas, covered bazaar, and library, as his finest work. The complex was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2011.

settings.threat.toggleHint: Phishing and malware addresses are checked on your device against open threat lists. The addresses you visit aren't sent to any server, including Google.

dialog.resetSettings.title: Reset settings
dialog.resetSettings.detail:
Will be reset: appearance, search engine, startup and home page, privacy and security settings, blocker level and exceptions, site permissions, accessibility.

Will be kept: bookmarks, history, saved passwords, QRtım session, VPN profiles, download folder, your sharing choices in Data and Privacy, and the consent records.

If account sync is on, the reset settings will also sync to your other devices.

dialog.clearData.message: All browsing data will be deleted
dialog.clearData.detail:
Will be deleted: cookies, site data, cache, visit log, download history (not the files), site permission decisions, and saved session.

Won't be deleted: bookmarks, saved passwords, settings, and VPN profiles.

This can't be undone.

diagConsent.title: Error reporting
diagConsent.message: İlgezdi ran into a problem. Send an error report?
diagConsent.detail:
The report only contains the app's own error information: version, operating system, error message, and recent events.

The addresses you visit, page titles, cookies, and passwords are NOT INCLUDED IN THE REPORT — addresses are converted into a label that can't be reversed.

Your decision is remembered; you can change it in Settings › Diagnostics.

data.title: Data and Privacy
data.subtitle: Your data stays on your device. You decide what gets shared, and every switch you turn on or off is written to the consent records below.
data.summary: Features that connect out: {on} of {total} on
data.settingsHint: See on one page which data stays on your device and which goes where, and manage each one separately.
data.saved: Saved and written to the consent records.
data.sec.deviceLead: This data is kept only on this computer and is never sent to a server.
data.sec.ilgezdiLead: These features connect to the internet to work. None of them sends the addresses you visit.
data.sec.accountLead: Sync only works when you're signed in with your QRtım account. You choose what syncs, and anything you turn off is also cleared from your account.
data.sec.ulgenLead: Ülgen runs on this computer: it doesn't connect to the internet or use a language model. Everything here is off by default. Ülgen works only with the permissions you turn on here, and you can take them back at any time.
data.sec.sitesLead: Limits what the sites you visit can learn about you.
data.sec.thirdPartyLead: You picked these services. We show them here so you know what they receive.
data.sec.logLead: Every switch you turn on or off here or in Settings is recorded with the date, version and device. Each record is linked to the one before it, so verification shows if anything was changed later. Records stay only on this device and aren't deleted when you reset settings.
data.item.visitLog.title: Visit log
data.item.visitLog.desc: Pages you visit are stored encrypted on this device. The History page and address bar suggestions use this log.
data.item.omniboxHistory.title: Suggestions from history in the address bar
data.item.omniboxHistory.desc: As you type, pages you've visited and your bookmarks are suggested. What you type is never sent anywhere.
data.item.restoreSession.title: Remember open tabs
data.item.restoreSession.desc: Tabs that are open when you close İlgezdi are saved on this device and come back next time. Private window tabs aren't saved.
data.item.savePasswords.title: Offer to save passwords
data.item.savePasswords.desc: When you sign in to a site, İlgezdi offers to save the password in the encrypted vault on your device.
data.item.clearHistoryOnExit.title: Clear history on exit
data.item.clearHistoryOnExit.desc: When İlgezdi closes, the visit log, download history and site icons are deleted.
data.item.clearSiteDataOnExit.title: Clear site data on exit
data.item.clearSiteDataOnExit.desc: When İlgezdi closes, cookies, site data and the cache are deleted. You'll be signed out of sites.
data.item.diagnostics.title: Error reports
data.item.diagnostics.desc: When something goes wrong, an anonymized technical report is sent to İlgezdi. Addresses you visit and personal information aren't included.
data.item.diagnostics.unasked: Not asked yet: you'll be asked after the first error. You can decide now instead.
data.item.updateCheck.title: Check for updates automatically
data.item.updateCheck.desc: At startup and every 6 hours, İlgezdi checks GitHub for a new version; only the version file is requested. When this is off, you can still check manually in Settings › General.
data.item.threatLists.title: Download harmful site lists
data.item.threatLists.desc: Harmful site lists are downloaded once a day and matching happens on your device. Addresses you visit aren't sent. When this is off, harmful site protection doesn't work.
data.item.discoverFeed.title: Update the Discover list
data.item.discoverFeed.desc: The app list on the Discover page comes from the İlgezdi website. When this is off, the list that ships with the app is shown.
data.item.syncSettings.title: Sync my settings
data.item.syncSettings.desc: Theme, search engine, privacy and blocker settings are saved to your QRtım account. Device-specific settings (VPN, download folder) aren't sent.
data.item.syncBookmarks.title: Sync my bookmarks
data.item.syncBookmarks.desc: Your bookmarks and folders are saved to your QRtım account. Turning this off also clears the copy in your account.
data.item.syncPasswords.title: Sync my passwords
data.item.syncPasswords.desc: This will be end-to-end encrypted, so the server can't read your passwords. It's coming with the QRtım subscription.
data.item.syncHistory.title: Sync my history
data.item.syncTabs.title: Sync my open tabs
data.item.syncTabs.desc: Coming together with sending tabs between devices.
data.item.ulgenChat.title: Let Ülgen process what I write
data.item.ulgenChat.desc: What you type to Ülgen is processed by Ülgen on this computer; it isn't sent to any server or stored. Required to use Ülgen.
data.item.ulgenPage.title: Share the open page without asking
data.item.ulgenPage.desc: When this is on, Ülgen reads the open page without asking to summarize it or search in it; when it's off, Ülgen asks every time. Page text isn't stored and the page's images aren't downloaded.
data.item.ulgenHistory.title: Personalize from my browsing history
data.item.ulgenHistory.desc: When you ask Ülgen to search your history, it searches your encrypted visit log; results appear only in the panel. Off in private windows.
data.item.ulgenInterests.title: Learn my interests
data.item.ulgenInterests.desc: A few of the most frequent words on pages you summarize are kept as interest tags on this computer, encrypted with your operating system's vault (up to 60 tags). Addresses and page text aren't kept; turning this off deletes the tags.
data.item.ulgenAccount.title: Save my Ülgen data to my QRtım account
data.item.ulgenAccount.desc: Once your QRtım account is connected, your interest tags can be saved to your account so Ülgen recognizes you on other devices too. Nothing is sent right now.
data.item.ulgenRecommend.title: Recommend products and content for me
data.item.ulgenRecommend.desc: TrendTech products and content suggestions may be shown based on your interests. Ülgen doesn't make recommendations right now.
data.item.ulgenImprove.title: Use my chats to improve Ülgen
data.item.ulgenImprove.desc: Chat samples separated from your identity may be used to improve Ülgen. No chats are stored or sent right now.
data.account.signedIn: You're signed in with your QRtım account; the types you chose are syncing.
data.account.signedOut: You're not signed in, so nothing is syncing right now. Your choices apply once you sign in.

data.tp.dnsAuto: If your system's DNS provider supports it, domain lookups are encrypted; otherwise they go to your internet provider.
data.tp.dnsOff: Secure DNS is off: the domain names of sites you open are looked up with your internet provider without encryption.
data.tp.pwnedDesc: Runs only when you press the button. Have I Been Pwned receives just the first 5 characters of each password's hash.
data.tp.vpnDesc: When it's on, all your traffic goes through the WireGuard server you chose.
